articles.title: Reading for pleasure isn’t just passing the time — psychology links it to lower stress and reduced dementia risk
articles.summary: Treating leisure reading as mere downtime misses its link to cognitive reserve and lower dementia risk in later life. Research reviewed in Psychological Medicine suggests a daily book habit—or a book club—is tied to sharper thinking and less loneliness as we age.

articles.title: Declining public healthcare access fuels lasting support for populist right parties in England
articles.summary: When local medical clinics close in England, nearby residents report worse care and become more likely to back populist right parties, suggests a study in American Political Science Review. The shift is strongest in high-immigration areas.

articles.title: Long-term singlehood doesn’t follow a single emotional script — a psychology study of 2,930 adults tracked how solo life unfolds over 11 years
articles.summary: Wanting a relationship—or feeling mixed about being single—doesn't mean your overall happiness is sliding downward. New psychology research tracking 2,930 never-married adults across 11 years found that roughly 90 percent maintained relatively high, steady life satisfaction even as their romantic and sexual feelings varied widely.

articles.title: Frontiers: A Roundtable Discussion on the I-Frame vs. S-Frame Debate
articles.summary: Applied behavioral scientists believe their work can influence people’s lives for the better. But what is the most effective way to make that happen? Is it through interventions focused on influencing individual behavior while maintaining freedom of choice? Is it by changing policies and laws, and thereby the systems, that individuals operate within? Is it a combination of the two? Is the distinction between an individual- or systems-focus a helpful one? Or, is the world too messy and complex? How should applied behavioral scientists navigate the financial and political influences on the work

articles.title: New nose drops restore youthful memory and fight Alzheimer’s in aging mice
articles.summary: A revolutionary new nasal treatment has restored youthful learning and memory performance in aging mice while preventing severe cognitive decline in mice with Alzheimer’s-like disease. Developed using technology similar to COVID-19 mRNA vaccines, the nose drops stimulate production of a brain-protecting protein that strengthens neurons and supports memory. Remarkably, the treatment preserved brain function without removing Alzheimer’s-associated plaques, suggesting a completely different way to combat cognitive decline.

articles.title: Mice slept 70% less after scientists switched off these brain cells
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered brain cells that actively generate the irresistible urge to sleep, and shutting them down allowed mice to sleep 70% less than normal. Remarkably, many of the animals avoided the severe behavioral consequences of sleep deprivation, raising intriguing possibilities for future sleep research.

articles.title: How education and marriage patterns shape household wealth in urban China
articles.summary: A recent study of urban Chinese households reveals that couples sharing similar educational backgrounds accumulate wealth differently, with dual-college marriages leading to the highest net worth and highlighting new patterns of economic inequality.

articles.summary: In a double-blind experiment, healthy adults given the ADHD stimulant methylphenidate cheated far less when nobody was watching, pointing to an unexpected moral side effect of a widely used "smart drug."

articles.title: New psychiatry review finds little consensus on which conditions count as “neurodivergent”
articles.summary: A new JAMA Psychiatry review of 134 studies finds scientists apply "neurodivergent" to 24 distinct diagnoses, from autism and ADHD to anxiety and stroke, raising concerns that broad umbrella labels can mask specific clinical needs.

articles.title: SAMA: Training-Free Consensus Ridge Tracking for Camera-Based Heart Rate on Five Public Datasets
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28185v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) is usually benchmarked by one heart rate per video, a figure that hides the short windows in which a tele-consultation would actually read the pulse. We present SAMA, a training-free estimator that (i) forms a quality-weighted consensus of POS and CHROM chrominance spectra, (ii) discounts frequencies occupied by pulse-free references derived from the same frames (frame motion, skin-mask geometry and background brightness), (iii) follows the heart rate through time with a Viterbi ridge under a random-walk prior,

articles.title: torchtsetlin: Fast, Interpretable Tsetlin Machines for PyTorch
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28195v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Tsetlin machine learns propositional rules with teams of Tsetlin automata that are driven by reward and penalty rather than gradients, so its models are interpretable by construction and cheap to evaluate. Its software, however, consists of C and CUDA kernels behind scikit-learn-style wrappers that sit outside the deep learning ecosystem. torchtsetlin implements the Tsetlin machine family as ordinary PyTorch modules: vanilla and weighted, coalesced, regression, convolutional over sequences, images and volumes, and dense per-pixel segmentation

articles.title: From Point Clouds to Engineering Models: Benchmarking Agentic 3D Reconstruction in the Built Environment
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28197v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coding agents can translate 3D measurements into CAD geometry, but reconstructing engineering models for the built environment demands semantic interpretation and consistent construction constraints beyond surface fitting. We formulate scene-level Scan-to-BIM (Building Information Modeling) as an agentic 3D coding task and introduce S2Bench, comprising public and proprietary scans of 128 real-world scenes across five domains, paired with expert-curated reference models spanning diverse spatial scales. A shared framework lets agents measure scans

articles.title: AutoPILOT: A Visual Agent Harness for Real-Time Gameplay
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28202v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multimodal foundation models can play video games well when the game waits for them, but often fail when it keeps running. We find that much of this gap lies in the harness, which decides what the model sees, what it remembers, and how its outputs become actions over time. Existing harnesses such as VISTA improve the first two, yet turn each model call into at most one action, so the agent acts only as often as its model thinks. We introduce AutoPILOT, which changes the third: in each model call, the model can send a primitive action, start an op
